summary: Testing coverage for CC-0116 is broad and well-layered: unit tests (reconcile_dbcredentials_test.go) cover the scoping helpers (table-driven same-name/diff-ns and diff-name/same-ns), the ExternalSecret builder, the managed create+gate path, idempotency, brownfield no-op (two dedicated tests), the readiness wait (both branches), and the ensure-error path; reconcile_keystone_test.go adds dedicated managed-override and brownfield-untouched secretRef tests; instrumentation_test.go adds a belt-and-suspenders condition-registration test; setupwithmanager_test.go covers Owns(ExternalSecret); integration_test.go adds a real ordering-gate test (Consistently Keystone NotFound until the ES syncs) plus a multi-CP distinct-paths test. Assertions are generally specific (function-derived AND literal anchors, no tautological constants). The one substantive issue is an OVERCLAIMING unit test: TestCredentialInvariant_DriveChainIncludesDBCredentialsBeforeKeystone — its name and docstring assert it proves DBCredentials runs BEFORE Keystone, but both of its assertions (the ES exists/owned, and Keystone.Spec.Database.SecretRef == dbCredentialSecretName(cp)) hold regardless of ordering, because reconcileKeystone computes that secretRef name as a pure deterministic function of cp with no read of the ExternalSecret. The genuine ordering gate is the integration test; the unit test's name/comment overstate its coverage (ensure-test-names-accurately-describe-coverage). No tier is missing (helm-unittest legitimately N/A: the DB credential is operator-generated, not a chart template; the unchanged externalsecrets ClusterRole rule is already asserted per the baseline).

tests_checklist.item: Unit tier present (reconcile_dbcredentials_test.go) covering helpers, builder, reconciler
Integration/envtest tier present (integration_test.go) with ordering + multi-CP tests
helm-unittest tier — N/A (DB credential is operator-generated, not a chart template; ClusterRole rule asserted unchanged per baseline)
Brownfield no-op has dedicated tests (BrownfieldNoExternalSecretReadyTrue, BrownfieldDoesNotRequeue, BrownfieldDBSecretRefUntouched)
Ordering gate Consistently assertion is real/non-vacuous (operator actively reconciling, Keystone provably absent without gate)
Table tests cover same-name/diff-ns and diff-name/same-ns
No tautological constant-only tests; assertions anchor both derived value and literal
e2e suite has presence-guard SKIP, wait_ready_condition, owner_of, and bao kv get of per-CP path

issues_found.description: TestCredentialInvariant_DriveChainIncludesDBCredentialsBeforeKeystone overclaims ORDERING. Its name and docstring assert it proves DBCredentials runs BEFORE Keystone ('which is only possible if DBCredentials ran before Keystone in the chain'), but neither of its two assertions actually distinguishes ordering. (1) The ES-existence/ownership check (es, ok := getDBCredentialES; OwnerReferences) only proves reconcileDBCredentials RAN at some point in the chain, not that it ran before reconcileKeystone. (2) The Keystone secretRef check k.Spec.Database.SecretRef.Name == dbCredentialSecretName(cp) is satisfied by reconcileKeystone ALONE: in managed mode reconcileKeystone sets keystone.Spec.Database.SecretRef = {Name: dbCredentialSecretName(cp), Key: "password"} as a pure deterministic function of cp (reconcile_keystone.go:121-122), with NO read of the ExternalSecret. If driveCredentialChain were reordered to call reconcileKeystone before reconcileDBCredentials, both assertions would still pass — so the test cannot detect the very regression its name promises. The real ordering gate is the integration test TestIntegration_FullReconcile_DBCredentialsBeforeKeystone (Consistently Keystone NotFound until the ES syncs). The unit test is still useful as a chain-wiring/secretRef-consumption check, but the name and docstring should be corrected to not claim it proves ordering.
issues_found.fix: Rename to reflect what it actually verifies (e.g. TestCredentialInvariant_DriveChainProjectsKeystoneAgainstDBCredentialSecret) and amend the docstring/inline comments at lines 310-317 and 338-339 to drop the 'only possible if DBCredentials ran before Keystone' ordering claim, instead pointing to TestIntegration_FullReconcile_DBCredentialsBeforeKeystone as the authoritative ordering proof. No production-code change needed.
issues_found.evidence: Test docstring line 339: '// possible if DBCredentials ran before Keystone in the chain (CC-0116, REQ-002).' and assertion lines 344-345: 'g.Expect(k.Spec.Database.SecretRef.Name).To(Equal(dbCredentialSecretName(cp)),' — while reconcile_keystone.go:121-122 sets 'keystone.Spec.Database.SecretRef = commonv1.SecretRefSpec{Name: dbCredentialSecretName(cp), Key: "password"}' purely from cp, never reading the ExternalSecret.

suggested_improvements: TestIntegration_FullReconcile_DBCredentialsBeforeKeystone uses a 2s Consistently window (line 692-693) while dbCredentialsRequeueAfter is 10s; the watch-triggered re-reconcile from the ES Create keeps Keystone absent, so the assertion holds, but a brief comment noting that the Owns(ExternalSecret) watch re-fires within the window (rather than relying solely on the 10s requeue) would make the non-vacuousness explicit to future maintainers.

Consider one negative integration assertion that the brownfield managed-vs-brownfield branch leaves Keystone.Spec.Database.SecretRef untouched end-to-end (currently brownfield secretRef behavior is unit-only via TestReconcileKeystone_BrownfieldDBSecretRefUntouched); not required, the unit coverage is adequate.
next_steps: Decide whether to rename/retag TestCredentialInvariant_DriveChainIncludesDBCredentialsBeforeKeystone and correct its docstring (ASK — purely a test-naming/comment accuracy change, no behavior change).
